limitations: Small offline samples; no release or venue acceptance.
Same repeated prompt can reuse KV cache; warm results are cache-warm, not independent new requests.
Queue and one-way network transfer lack separate server timestamps.
TCP submission time is local socket buffering, not proof of remote receipt.

results.scope: Layer 4 representative deterministic microbenchmark, not formal production release
results.coldCaveat: process-first only; OS disk/page caches not evicted; setup copied inputs immediately before execution
results.repeatProtocol: one process per host; first iteration plus 3 same-process warm repetitions, local batch then DGX batch
results.transferProtocol: SCP SSH handshake included, setup and remote tar preparation/extraction excluded; artifacts download separate from result receipt returned on stdout

macbook.scope: deterministic delivery microbenchmark only; no formal producer, model inference, deployment, HTTP, device or venue acceptance
macbook.warmDefinition: same Python process; no OS page-cache eviction; first is process-first, not guaranteed cold disk

dgxSpark.scope: deterministic delivery microbenchmark only; no formal producer, model inference, deployment, HTTP, device or venue acceptance
dgxSpark.warmDefinition: same Python process; no OS page-cache eviction; first is process-first, not guaranteed cold disk

transport.scope: four separate process invocations per host; paired Mac then DGX, previously copied inputs; remote input transfer excluded, complete receipt return included
notes: No server queue/model load/prefill/decode timing applies: deterministic worker only
round trip includes subprocess launch, Python startup, imports, processing, receipt serialization/return, plus SSH handshake/network for DGX
All requests may have warm OS file caches; first transport request is not a cold-device claim

limitations: Each dispatch contains exactly one newly loaded model inference; no result cache.
First-result event means complete result metadata received on the dispatcher; TTS PCM file arrives by separately measured SCP download.
Input and weights are reused from the original batch; no fresh input SCP or large model download.
Prior model hash receipts are reused without large-weight rehash; input hashes are recomputed.
New process does not mean uncached filesystem; operating system cache was not flushed.
Model precision/runtime differ as in the original batch.
